text:
Montreal controlled almost every minute of this game and still needed a shootout to get the two points. Olen Zellweger scored on a 2 percent chance in the first period and again early in the third, and Josh Norris added another 3 percent look, so Buffalo erased a 3-1 deficit in 61 seconds without generating much beyond a few long-shot goals. MTL finished with 3.46 expected goals to BUF's 2.11, 57 shot attempts to 42, and the simulated replays of every shot give the Canadiens a 73 percent chance of winning.

The gap came from the first two periods, where MTL out-chanced BUF 1.84 to 0.81 in expected goals. Lane Hutson scored on the power play late in the first, Cole Caufield made it 2-1 early in the second, and Josh Anderson stretched it to 3-1 with 50 seconds left in the period. Hutson logged 27:06 with 1.9 expected goals for against 0.89 against while he was on the ice. BUF went 0 for 5 on the power play, and Jacob Fowler faced only 16 shots, though he allowed three goals on 2.11 expected.

Buffalo's best stretch came in the third, when it out-chanced MTL 1.30 to 0.77, and Luukkonen stayed even with the game, stopping 35 of 38 shots. Noah Ostlund had a 29 percent look turned aside by Fowler. Montreal then took overtime 0.85 to 0.00 in expected goals. In the shootout, Caufield, Alexandre Texier and Zachary Bolduc scored for MTL, while Jack Quinn was stopped after Tage Thompson had matched Caufield in round one.
